title: Budgeted batching & deterministic replay — weekly sync
content:
Week: 2029-03-11 -> 2029-03-15
Owners: Maya Patel (notes), Ali Park (dispatcher), Samir Rao (kernel), Leah Kim (kv-cache)
Attendees: core runtime squad, oncall rotation (Owen), solutions eng observer (Priya)

Purpose: summarize work on the new budgeted-batching dispatcher heuristic, the deterministic-replay harness for nondeterministic batch failures, and KV cache soft-reserve experiments. Capture metrics, open questions, and rollout plan.

TL;DR:
- Implemented prototype of budgeted-batching in dispatcher; staging gate +10% traffic for soak next week.
- Deterministic-replay harness reduces flaky integration failures by reproducing request ordering and kernels with recorded scheduling stamps.
- KV-cache soft-reserve reduced long-session eviction by 22% at low memory pressure but increased fragmentation on older H100 driver builds.
- Overall P95 latency improved under 3x burst tests when combined with budgeted batching + backpressure shaping.

What we shipped this week
1) Dispatcher: budgeted-batching MVP
- New mode: budgeted-batching — dispatcher computes a token budget per batch based on per-route SLO and per-org cost budget hints.
- Heuristic: batch_budget = min(max_batch_tokens, floor(remaining_budget / estimate_cost_per_token)). When budget < small-batch-threshold the dispatcher favors lower-latency routing (fast-path single request).
- Integrations: works with the existing batcher queue, exposes two new runtime flags for canary: --budgeted-batching-enabled and --budgeted-batching-agg-window.
- Observations: small throughput regression (~2.8%) on synthetic uniform-token benchmarks (expected because we break up big bundles) but P95 tail under burst improved ~18%.

2) Deterministic-replay harness (debugging tool)
- Motivation: intermittent nondeterministic failures surfaced in nightly integration where kernel ordering + micro-batching changed numerical results causing evaluation drift. Difficult to reproduce locally.
- Approach: attach per-request scheduling stamps (arrival_seq, dispatcher_epoch, kernel_launch_seq) and capture minimal kernel inputs (KV cache snapshot diff + request tensors) for a faulty window. A replay runner can then deterministically restore the scheduling order and re-run kernels on the same hardware type.
- Results: reproduced 9/12 flaky cases from the past 6 weeks locally (previously unreproducible). Root causes found: two kernel kernel-launch races (race between prefetch eviction and kernel read) and an uninitialized padding path in a legacy kernel path that only manifests with certain micro-batch schedules.
- Next: add finer-grained capture for long KV snapshots and add toggle to anonymize payloads for privacy when requesting customer traces.

3) KV cache soft-reserve experiment
- Soft-reserve: keep a small percentage of slots (configurable per-tenant) that cannot be immediately evicted for short-lived sessions. Aims to reduce churn for interactive chat sessions that perform many short turns.
- Staging results: with soft-reserve = 8% we saw session eviction for long-lived chats drop by 22% and end-to-end perceived latency for those sessions drop ~12ms median.
- Regressions: fragmentation increased memory allocator churn on older H100 drivers (driver 520.x). No regression on latest drivers (545.x).
- Mitigation plan: two-pronged — (1) implement a periodic compaction pass during low-load windows, (2) pin soft-reserve to hardware families only when drivers are newer than 540.

Metrics snapshot (end-to-end, staging harness)
- Baseline (no budgeted batching): peak qps 120k, P50 45ms, P95 310ms, average tokens/sec per GPU 1.00x
- Budgeted-batching (canary env): peak qps 115k, P50 48ms, P95 255ms, tokens/sec per GPU 0.97x
- Budgeted + soft-reserve: peak qps 112k, P50 47ms, P95 240ms, long-session eviction -22%
- Deterministic replay reproduce rate on historical flakies: 75% (9/12)

Decisions made
- Enable budgeted-batching in staging at +10% routing for 48 hour soak starting 2029-03-18. If P95 stays <300ms and error budget not exceeded -> expand to +30% next week. (Owner: Ali Park)
- Do not enable soft-reserve by default for Dedicated customers until compaction pass implemented. Soft-reserve will be optional per-tenant. (Owner: Leah Kim)
- Add deterministic-replay collection to nightly flaky-capture job as opt-in for internal runs only. (Owner: Samir Rao)

Action items (owners + due dates)
- Ali: roll dispatcher flags to staging +10% and monitor p95 & error budget. (due 2029-03-18)
- Samir: land kernel fix for padding path and add unit test that asserts deterministic output for small-batch permutations. (due 2029-03-20)
- Leah: implement compaction pass prototype and add driver-family gating logic. (due 2029-03-25)
- Owen: extend deterministic replay to capture anonymized KV diffs; coordinate with security for acceptable telemetry. (due 2029-03-22)
- Priya: write short PR/notes for solutions eng to explain behavioral changes for customers relying on low-latency single-request flows. (due 2029-03-19)

Risks / open questions
- Cost model accuracy: estimate_cost_per_token is currently simple and can under/over-provision batches for very spiky routes. Next iteration will fit a per-route estimator using recent token distribution.
- Driver fragmentation: need to confirm fragmentation on other hardware (T4, V100) before rolling soft-reserve more broadly.
- Observability: current tracing stamps are low-cardinality; need to ensure trace sampling doesn't miss problematic windows.

Notes from micro-discussions
- Samir: "We should not assume clearing kernel-local tmp buffers is free — a zeroing path caused the padding bug."
- Ali: "The budgeted heuristic is deceptively powerful — we can shape both cost and latency if we tune the estimate model quickly."
- Leah: "Soft reserve helps UX for chat but it is effectively a small per-tenant memory reservation; we must expose clear billing implications to sales."

Staging run plan (recap)
- 2029-03-18 09:00 UTC: enable budgeted-batching +10% on staging dispatcher.
- 2029-03-18 09:15 UTC: begin synthetic 3x burst tests (15m cadence) and record p50/p95, cancellations, kernel failures.
- 2029-03-20 09:00 UTC: evaluate soak. If ok: expand to +30% and enable deterministic capture for flaky windows.

Links / references
- Budgeted batching RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SERV/Budgeted+Batching+RFC
- Kernel padding bug fix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/3482
- Jira: SERV-4721 (budgeted-batching), SERV-4803 (deterministic-replay), SERV-4810 (kv-soft-reserve)

Appendix: quick reproduction steps for deterministic replay
1) Enable "replay-capture" on the failing host (runtime flag).
2) Trigger the failing trace or capture from nightly flaky job.
3) Use replay-runner with --staging-image and --capture-id to replay on the same hardware family.
4) If reproduction succeeds, attach capture bundle to the PR and tag Samir for kernel triage.

——
Notes saved in working doc style; will consolidate into RFC if staging soak is successful.
